newsitem.title: ROMANIA: Explosion of Romania experimental bomb kills 16.
newsitem.headline: Explosion of Romania experimental bomb kills 16.

text.p: An experimental bomb exploded on Wednesday during a test at a military airfield in southern Romania, killing 16 workers and injuring two, officials said.
Constantin Dudu Ionescu, State Secretary for Defence, said the bomb had detonated as it was being loaded aboard a IAR-93 fighter-bomber in Craiova, 235 km (140 miles) west of the capital.

Television pictures showed several men in air force uniforms gathered around the charred wreckage of the aircraft at the edge of a runway. One body, burned virtually beyond recognition, lay nearby until the men took it away.
Ionescu said the device contained several smaller bombs inside its casing designed to explode in succession as it neared its target. A large fire broke out, but was extinguished within 20 minutes.

"The aircraft had made two test flights earlier in the day without the bomb on board," he said by telephone. "As the device was being loaded aboard the plane for a third flight with real ammunition, one of the bombs inside exploded."

Senior defence officials said 15 people died immediately from burns and shrapnel wounds and one man succumbed to his injuries soon after. Two others escaped with severe injuries but were out of danger in hospital.
The pilot had not yet gone aboard the aircraft, jointly produced in the 1970s by Romania and Yugoslavia but no longer manufactured.

The accident came a day after NATO's 16 leaders announced in Madrid that Romania's bid for early membership of the security alliance had failed but left the door open for a review of further expansion in 1999 and specifically praised the efforts of Romania.
Ionescu had earlier told a briefing at government headquarters in Bucharest there was no explanation yet for the explosion, but he said it could have been due to technical failure.
He said the dead included defence industry workers and military engineers.
Ionescu told reporters the device had been produced at the Mija defence plant in Ploiesti, north of Bucharest.
"Tests will continue as this is one of the most modern types of ammunition we have," he said.

A defence ministry statement, quoted by the official Rompres news agency, said the test was being conducted as part of procedures to secure a licence for the device, described as "a new type of aviation ammunition".
A government commission had arrived in Craiova to investigate the causes of the explosion.
